patches.name: hwa_rx_stop_abort_timeout_without_debug
patches.rationale: On an RX-completion drain timeout with error logging disabled, return through the existing epilogue instead of proceeding to RX-post reinitialization with outstanding completions.

patches.name: hwa_rx_stop_abort_timeout_after_logging
patches.rationale: After logging an RX-completion drain timeout, return through the existing epilogue instead of proceeding to RX-post reinitialization with outstanding completions. Persistent failure can leave firmware RX paused; this does not force hardware recovery.

patches.name: hwa_reinit_status_to_guard
patches.rationale: Route the RX-post reinitialization result to its dedicated status guard, keeping the original notifier call and all arguments unchanged.

patches.name: hwa_rxpost_update_to_shared_epilogue
patches.rationale: After the unchanged RX-post update call, return through the existing complete epilogue rather than the repurposed duplicate epilogue.

patches.name: hwa_rxpost_restore_pub_argument
patches.rationale: Restore the public DHD argument in the shared successful/non-offloaded update path.

patches.name: hwa_rxpost_call_original_update
patches.rationale: Enter the unchanged relocated RX-post update call after restoring its public DHD argument.

patches.name: hwa_rxpost_abort_reinit_failure
patches.rationale: On any nonzero RX-post reinitialization status, return through the complete existing epilogue before RX-post update can issue its hardware doorbell.

patches.name: hwa_rxpost_success_to_argument_restore
patches.rationale: After successful RX-post reinitialization, continue to the shared argument restore and unchanged update call.

patches.name: hwa_rxpost_nonoffload_early_bypass_status
patches.rationale: The non-offloaded capability-disabled path has no reinitialization status; branch directly to argument restore without interpreting unrelated register contents.

patches.name: hwa_rxpost_nonoffload_shared_bypass_status
patches.rationale: The non-offloaded shared-index path must preserve its update even if the prior void writer leaves a nonzero register value.

patches.name: hwa_rxpost_nonoffload_dma_bypass_status
patches.rationale: The non-offloaded DMA-index path must preserve its update even if the prior void writer leaves a nonzero register value.

rationale: The original scheduler advances a cached host reader without consuming Runner-owned RX completions. Use the actual DMA/shared consumer and producer indices for a non-consuming scheduling check, preserving TX behavior and the existing Runner ipend notification guard. The existing watchdog supplies periodic RX-only retries under the original perimeter lock after active-state rechecks, without adding a timer or extending protocol lifetime. This repairs retry suppression when the cached reader catches the producer; it does not prove the initiating hardware stall or guarantee recovery from every loss of progress. HWA RX stop recovery now aborts on drain timeout and on nonzero RX-post reinitialization status; success and non-offloaded paths retain the original calls and arguments without changing relocation slots.

reinit_guard_control_flow.note: The nine instruction replacements reuse a duplicate epilogue; both existing CALL26 relocations and zero-valued notification arguments stay unchanged. Direct non-offloaded entrances bypass the status guard.
